note: The same shape as most of this batch: the starting-point criteria hold and the commercial ones fail. Good to great is unambiguous — 27, 71 kg at 180 cm, described by the rep as already lean and agreeing, with strength as the goal and physique explicitly secondary: 'once I start and feel stronger, then my physique will also change, but I think that's secondary.' Not deconditioned holds on both halves: lean, runs a two-mile circuit before training, uses an outdoor calisthenics gym, and is not remotely gym-averse. Neglected health holds in substance — he was sedentary for his first year in Italy, smoked cannabis for ten years, and is three to four months into addressing it, so health is the neglected area now being picked up rather than a crisis. Successful fails: a telemetry analyst for a go-kart team, invoicing job to job, is not the business-owner or physician profile the stated ICP names. Income fails decisively and by his own careful accounting — one to two thousand available, two months with no work booked, a first-year tax bill larger than budgeted, and a principle he stated twice: 'even with financing, I think it wouldn't be financially responsible.' Two things for the rollup. First, the rep reached the same conclusion live and disqualified rather than discounted, which is the behaviour the ICP is supposed to produce and rarely does elsewhere in this batch. Second, this is an outbound-sourced lead — Trevor contacted him, not the reverse — and the prospect said so when asked why he had taken the meeting at all. An ICP screen cannot help if the pipeline is generating prospects who never went looking.
